results.title: Rebuilding of wartime museum in Reyðarfjörður well under way
results.description: Work to rebuild Stríðsárasafnið in Reyðarfjörður is well advanced. The museum suffered extensive storm damage in 2022, when two huts were completely destroyed. New huts are now being built in their place. The museum has been operating since 1995. Visitors can learn about the British and American occupation of Iceland during the Second World War, when one of their main bases was in Reyðarfjörður. Þórhildur Tinna Sigurðardóttir, director of the museum and Fjarðabyggð's cultural office, says the museum has had exhibitions since it was founded, but the exhibition had remained unchanged until now. That is why the damage presented a unique opportunity to rethink and redesign the exhibitions based on the collection we have... This has all moved very quickly and has been a joint effort by us in Fjarðabyggð and the town council. An open meeting will be held in the hut that has remained standing throughout, giving visitors an insight into the ideas behind the project. Sara Hjördís Blöndal is designing the new exhibition. "Recently, the work has mainly involved going through the collection and the storage areas, seeing what we have and piecing the exhibition together from that," Sara says. It is incredible to see everything being built up here again, and it will be great to meet people at the meeting.
